messages:
Leo: quick sketch — we need a 'soft eviction' priority model for variant fallback when capacity is tight. goal: prefer enterprise/committed tenants, prefer low-cost regions, but also avoid starving long-waiting requests. thinking API shape: per-plan defaults + optional per-tenant overrides + region adjustments. any strong objections?
Anya: //+1 on algo but we need decision-level telemetry. each routing decision must emit: score components, selected_variant, fallback_reason. otherwise debugging will be impossible.
Samir: agree on telemetry. also propose DSL instead of ad-hoc weights. example: 
```json
{ "priorityExpr": "0.6 * commitment_level + 0.25 * (1 - region_cost_norm) + 0.15 * request_age_norm",
  "plans": {
    "free": { "commitment_level": 0.1 },
    "pro": { "commitment_level": 0.5 },
    "enterprise": { "commitment_level": 1.0 }
  }
}
```
This lets us evolve logic without breaking backward compat.
Maria: two concerns: 1) quotas — do we prefer soft-eviction or strict quota enforcement? mixing both can be surprising to customers. 2) UI — console presets for common expressions, and a preview tool that simulates decisions for a sample tenant.
ops-bot: rollout-ci: policy-compiler unit tests passed (branch: priority-dsl) :white_check_mark:
Anya: recommended rollout: feature-flag + canary by tenant_class and region (start enterprise in us-west). dashboards: add a 'fallback heatmap' (region x plan) + a per-request decision detail view.
Leo: love the DSL idea. action items: @Samir to own the API + telemetry schema, @Maria to prototype console preview UX, @Anya to draft rollout plan. I can take the regression tests for cost/latency. tagging for visibility :eyes:
